findings.reason: §1's done-when says "every module under nova/" and §4 makes deletion depend on that coverage, so the brief must either measure with omit disabled (recording the reason) or name both packages as excluded from deletion; without that the plan's own negative control cannot distinguish "unreached" from "not measured".
findings.text: §1 requires "for every module under nova/, the lines executed by each route against its total", but the repository's configured coverage run omits `nova/.../scripts/*` and `nova/.../utilities/*` (pyproject.toml:321-324), so a route measured through the configured mechanism reports those packages as absent (not merely zero), and §4 deletes modules "that §1 shows unreached by either route" — so a module in either omitted package that a live lane or a public entry point reaches would read as unreached and be deleted while still live

findings.reason: the plan names no enumerator, so this changes only the node brief; it is recorded here because the brief must carry the owner and the positive-control requirement, and a census whose candidate list is empty must fail rather than pass.
findings.text: §2 must enumerate every Python file under benchmarks/ and scripts/ and make the union of verdicts equal the measured total, and the repository already owns a tree enumeration with a positive control: `worktree_path_candidates()` at nova/database/filepath.py:254, used exactly this way in tests/test_artifacts_carry_no_worktree_paths.py:25, which asserts a known-present path is in the candidate set so an empty scan cannot read as a clean tree — a second enumerator beside it will drift from the tracked-file definition (`git ls-files` semantics, deletions, untracked scratch) that the owner already handles

findings.reason: the plan's §2 negative control and §5 register are already implemented idioms in this repository, so the brief should hand those nodes the existing census/refusal pattern rather than let each author its own, and the plan's own text should stop implying a new census mechanism is needed.
findings.text: §2's "covers every file" and "a driver a live test imports, forced to a delete verdict, is refused and named" is the same shape as the existing recovery-ladder census, and the existing implementation already delivers both halves: benchmarks/recovery_ladder_census.py enumerates by convention and raises naming a renamed entry, with tests/test_recovery_ladder_census.py:20-30 pinning the enumeration to the module and the refusal to a monkeypatched deletion, while scripts/iron_operator_bound/reuse_check.py:1 is the existing ast-based scan that "refuses a second implementation of a block this repair gave one owner" over scripts/ and tests/ — which is the mechanism §5's register and the `hot-path-guard` decision would otherwise author a third time

findings.reason: the plan is about an endpoint, not a helper, but the brief must route revision stamping through the existing owner and must state that a census which re-shells to git per file duplicates it; recording it here keeps the duplicate from being introduced in the node's own text.
findings.text: §1 done-when 3 ("the record states the revision measured") and §2 done-when 2 ("the revision that record ran at, and that revision resolves") need a revision stamp and a path-relative-to-repository identity; `compute_provenance()` at nova/database/filepath.py:356 and `repository_relative()` at :397 are the owners of generated-artifact identity and repository-relative naming, while roughly twenty scripts currently hand-roll their own git invocation (for example scripts/iron_limb_production/measure.py and scripts/diiid_map_fidelity/measure.py each resolve revision through their own subprocess call)

findings.reason: §6's endpoint is "the one public forward route, module by module", and reconciling it with the existing kernel-launch trace is a semantic obligation; the brief needs to say which instrument is authoritative for ordering and which for cost, and that a module absent from the line map but present in the kernel trace is a contradiction to report, not a zero to delete on.
findings.text: the plan's §0 quotes the 2026-11-13 H200 profile ("about 12,500 kernel launches per slice") and §1 then measures the route a second way (Python line execution), but the existing evidence already attributes the forward route by device kernel (bank-solve-trace.html: the per-solve device attribution table, produced by scripts/prototypes/bank_solve_profile/report.py:14) and by route rows (bank-route-rows.html), so two instruments now describe "the route" with no stated relation, and §6 must reconcile them or the documented route will contradict the devicetrace that §0 relies on

findings.reason: the plan names no launch recipe, so this is a brief-level reuse note; it is recorded because the brief must name the existing launcher and the partition, and a manifest whose gate ran a home-made recipe should be treated as a scope defect.
findings.text: §3 and §4 require the suite delta "run on all_debug", and §1 requires an all_debug job, while scripts/nova_lane/run.sh and scripts/h200_test_lane/run.sh already own partition submission, interpreter invocation without uv on a compute node, and log shape; a node composing its own srun recipe replays the environment hazards the launchers encode (TMPDIR, NO_SYNC etc.)

response_events.note: The s1 brief measures with the coverage omit list disabled (an explicit --rcfile or omit override), and records that nova/scripts and nova/utilities were measured; the s4 brief refuses deletion of any module the s1 record marks as not measured rather than zero.

reuse_search-1.note: The s1 brief measures with the coverage omit list disabled (an explicit --rcfile or omit override), and records that nova/scripts and nova/utilities were measured; the s4 brief refuses deletion of any module the s1 record marks as not measured rather than zero.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each section's endpoint is one stored record (or one documented section) that carries the map, the verdicts and the revision behind a single artifact, rather than a spread of per-file wrappers; §1, §2 and §5 each produce one record that the later nodes read as data.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the census enumerator, the provenance/revision stamp and the "refuse a second implementation of an owned block" scan all already have owners (nova/database/filepath.py, benchmarks/recovery_ladder_census.py, scripts/iron_operator_bound/reuse_check.py), and the plan's §2, §5 and §1 each imply a fresh one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds a public definition, a CLI option, an MCP view or a refusal family, and §6 edits an existing document section rather than exposing new surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §1 measures executed lines per module with no mechanism named, while coverage.py is already a declared dependency (pyproject.toml:92) with a configured run and report section whose omit list hides two whole packages under nova/.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section proposes a wrapper around existing machinery; the four code-bearing endpoints are a measurement, a census, a batch deletion and a document section, none of which forwards without adding behaviour.
